extracted.intended_audience: writers, agents, editors, publishers and other members of the Absolute Write online community
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for posting, sharing work, and participating in the Absolute Write Water Cooler community (what you may post, how to post, and site-specific rules). Applies to writers seeking critique, discussion, or community on Absolute Write.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-tolerance policy for AI-generated or AI-assisted content
rubrics_metrics.description: We have a strict zero-tolerance policy for anything AI-generated or AI-assisted, be it creative writing, forum posts, graphics or even your avatar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of any material that has been generated with the assistance of AI will be deleted, and the member using it banned.

rubrics_metrics.name: AW Writing Lab: only original, unpublished work intended for critique
rubrics_metrics.description: This area is for posting work for sharing and critting. Only original work that is unpublished and intended for critique may be posted here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read 'Intro to Share Your Work | Posting and Critting' and the forum guidelines and info you need to read before posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the Newbie Guide / FAQs / stickies before posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Many boards instruct new users to read the Newbie Guide, FAQs, and board stickies before posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on the page: 'Please read The Newbie Guide to Absolute Write', 'Frequently Asked Questions', 'Read the Stickies, especially this one.' Follow board-specific stickies and first-post instructions (e.g., 'Post the First Three Sentences' thread: '[PLEASE READ FIRST POST]').

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and valid email required to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: Want to participate? Register for a free account. The email you register with us must be valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you can't log in you may need to reset your password and check your email (and spam folder). Use the Contact Us button if problems persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for existing/related threads before posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before creating a new thread in many boards, users are asked to search for similar topics and existing threads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit example: Research board — 'Be sure to search for similar topics before posting.' Office Party also asks users to 'please check for existing threads' before starting a new one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Writing Questions (BWQs) — no fiction or poetry posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic Writing Questions are general in nature and are not for posting fiction or poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BWQs are for perennial questions from new writers or those reaching a new stage; 'Do not post fiction or poetry here.' Read the Introduction and other stickies for the board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Party posting etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Before starting a new thread in Office Party, check for existing threads and focus on positive things rather than 'things we hate'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please do not start display threads in Office Party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry board is not a display site
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the place to discuss the writing, reading, publishing, and appreciation of all forms of poetry. This is not a display site for poems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use poetry-specific subforums for activities like 'Poetry Games and Exercises' or 'Poetry Chapbook' as directed by the board stickies.

rubrics_metrics.name: From Other Forums: no dissing other message boards or moderators
rubrics_metrics.description: When posting in 'From Other Forums and Message Boards', do not diss other message boards or moderators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check board description and follow its civility rule when posting updates or setting up temporary refugee camps during outages of other forums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bio/Autobio/Memoir board restriction: no legal questions
rubrics_metrics.description: This board is for writing about real people; no legal questions, please.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need legal advice, seek an appropriate forum or professional counsel rather than posting in the memoir board.

rubrics_metrics.name: W1/S1 (Write 1 | Sub 1) forum purpose and participation expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Write 1 | Sub 1 is for those committed to write one piece and submit one — a place to spread your wings for writers maintaining a production/submission habit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board supports a discipline of producing and submitting work (e.g., 'Whether it's a novel a year or a flash piece a day — write one, submit one'). Follow that community's conventions and stickies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flash Fiction forum status (read-only/archive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flash Fiction is no longer active. This forum is read-only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not post new material in forums explicitly marked read-only; consult subforum listings for active places to submit flash fiction or archives for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow board-specific scope and format guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each board defines its scope (genre, format, allowed content) and may have sub-forums for particular activities (e.g., Screenwriting tech room, Submitting and Selling Flash Fiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before posting, check the specific board description and sub-forums to ensure your topic belongs (examples throughout the forum listing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be civil and supportive; community norms emphasize courtesy
rubrics_metrics.description: Community areas emphasize mutual support (e.g., 'Be Excellent To One Another') and have norms around encouragement, dealing with rejection, and sharing goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forums like 'Be Excellent To One Another', 'Goals and Accomplishments', and 'Rejection and Dejection' for supportive conversation; follow moderators' guidance and board-specific civility rules.
